title: Fixed Beveled Twin Rules and Oblique Link Pair
description: One newly authored complete paired-parallel-rule-inspired instrument in a fixed offset open pose. Two whole equally broad and equally long wooden-look straightedge bodies each have one continuous flat ground face, two genuinely sloping long edge bevels and a low central turned grasp knob. Two complete short round-ended oblique metal-look links span the gap at separated positions; four entire headed vertical pins join those links to the two broad rule bodies. The long external straightedges remain parallel in this one authored pose, and the centre between the links is a genuinely open through-window rather than a filled plate or drawing board. All blade sections, full end faces, link outlines, pin and knob profiles and numerical layout are original. Unlike the board-mounted copying pantograph, the two complete broad ground-contact straightedge bodies are themselves the main tool, not thin four-bar rods suspended from an origin pedestal, with an extended copying arm, two styli and a support board. Unlike the sliding bevel, neither long body is a forked stock or a slotted blade turning about one end. No old pantograph components are deleted, reduced, transformed or reused; no old ruler mesh is imported. Ten closed editable whole meshes and four opaque constant untextured PBR roles, metres native Z up and full horizontal-bounds-centred ground datum. One original model zero scenes, not two ruler assets. Unmarked generic navigational-drafting category art, not a named maker, museum replica, historic scale or ivory material. The pins intentionally enter solid bodies as fixed joins; no free bearings, articulation, sliding or trajectory is claimed.
